transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Yeah… hi. I guess what brings me in is, I can’t really keep my words in a straight line anymore. Like, I’ll start trying to explain something simple, like something that happened on an overnight shift, and then somehow I’m talking about soccer, or the color of the walls, or paint colors I saw somewhere, or patient charts, and by the time I look at the person I can tell they’re lost. Like their face changes, and I realize I’ve dragged them through five different things and I don’t even know exactly how I got there.

It’s frustrating because in my head it feels connected at first, like there’s a path, but then when it comes out loud it’s all mixed up. I’ll be trying to answer one question, and then I hear myself saying something else, and then I try to fix it, but that makes it longer and worse. People kind of wait for me to get back to the point, and I can see that happening, and then I get more tangled. That’s the main reason I came in, I think.
Have you been feeling unusually high or euphoric lately?

Um… unusually high, like happy-high? I don’t think so. Not really. I mean, I’ve had moments where I’m maybe more wound up or I’m talking a lot, but euphoric doesn’t sound right to me. I don’t feel like everything is great or like I’m on top of the world.

If anything, when people say “high,” I think of someone being excited or confident or like… bright, I guess, and that’s not how it feels from the inside. I’m not sure I’d call it that. Maybe I’m misunderstanding what you mean by euphoric, but no, I haven’t noticed feeling especially good in that way.
Have you been hearing voices when no one is there?

I don’t… I don’t think so? Not like a clear voice standing behind me or someone talking in the room when I can look and nobody’s there. I mean, sometimes I get unsure because places can be noisy, especially at work, and you hear carts or people down the hall or someone calling for someone, and then it turns out maybe it wasn’t what I thought. But I wouldn’t say I’ve been hearing voices exactly.

Like, if you mean words, actual words, telling me things or talking to me, I don’t think I have that. Sometimes my own thoughts are loud, if that makes sense, but they feel like mine. So… no, not that I’ve noticed.
Have you felt sure that someone is trying to harm you or plot against you?

Yeah… I mean, “harm” sounds maybe too dramatic if you mean like someone physically attacking me, but… yes, I do feel like something is going on at work. I’m pretty sure the supervisors have been changing my shifts on purpose, and not just because of staffing like they keep saying. They’ll say, “Oh, we’re short,” or “We had to move people around,” but it keeps happening in a way that feels directed at me.

And the cameras on the unit… I know they’re there for safety, obviously, but I feel like they’re watching me through them specifically, like checking if I’m unsafe or waiting for me to mess up. I’ll be walking down the hall and I can feel myself thinking, okay, they’re looking right now, they’re seeing how I’m moving, how I’m talking to people, whether I look off. People tell me it’s just normal cameras and normal scheduling, but it doesn’t feel random to me. It feels like they’re building some kind of case or testing me without saying it directly.
Have you had a period when you needed much less sleep than usual and still felt full of energy?

I don’t think so. I mean, my sleep is not great sometimes, but needing much less sleep and then feeling full of energy… that doesn’t really sound like me.

If I don’t sleep much, I usually feel it. I’m tired, kind of dragging, more on edge maybe, but not energized like I can just keep going and don’t need rest. There might be nights where I’m up later than I meant to be, or I wake up and can’t get settled again, but the next day I’m not like, “Wow, I’m fine.” I’m more trying to get through the day.

So… no, I haven’t noticed a period like that where I barely slept and still felt really powered up or anything.
Did these problems start after a head injury, seizure, or another medical illness?

I don’t think so… not that I can connect it to. I mean, I’ve never sat down and thought, “Okay, this all started right after I hit my head,” or after a seizure or some illness like that. I don’t really have a clear thing like that in my mind.

I guess I’m not totally sure what would count, because people get sick sometimes or have headaches or whatever, but nothing stands out to me like a major medical thing that came first and then everything changed right after. So… as far as I know, no, I haven’t noticed that kind of connection.
Apart from your concerns about work, do you have any other strong beliefs that people say are not true?

Not really apart from that… I mean, that’s the main thing people keep telling me I’m “reading into,” but it doesn’t feel like I’m making it up.

It’s mostly work. The supervisors changing my shifts, and then the cameras on the unit. People say it’s just staffing shortages or that the cameras are just normal safety cameras, and I understand that’s what they’re supposed to be for, but it feels too specific to me. Like it’s not just random scheduling or normal monitoring. It feels like they’re watching to see if I’m unsafe, or if I’ll do something wrong, or like they’re gathering something on me.

So… if you mean other beliefs like outside of work, I don’t know. Nothing comes to mind the same way. It’s mainly that situation, but it feels very real to me even when other people say it isn’t.
Have you noticed yourself becoming less interested in being around other people?

Yeah… I have. I’ve kind of pulled away from people a lot, more than I even like admitting, I guess.

I used to be more… I don’t know, involved. Like I used to sketch murals, just for fun, and I’d get really into the ideas for them. I used to cook for friends too — not anything fancy all the time, but I liked having people over, making food, hanging out. And on weekends I’d play soccer, or at least I’d make plans to. It wasn’t like I was some super social person every second, but I had things I cared about, and people I’d actually want to see.

Now it all just feels kind of pointless. Like someone texts me and I’ll see it, and I know I should answer, but I just… don’t. Then hours go by, or days, and it feels harder to respond because now I have to explain why I didn’t. So I just ignore it. I end up staying in my apartment most of the time.

It’s not always that I hate people or anything. It’s more like being around them feels like too much effort, and the things I used to enjoy don’t really pull me in anymore. I know that sounds bad, but that’s kind of how it’s been.
Have other people told you that your face or voice seems less expressive than it used to be?

I’m not really sure. Nobody’s sat me down and said, “Your face looks flat,” or “Your voice sounds different,” not in those exact words.

I mean, sometimes people will say I seem tired, or they’ll ask if I’m okay because I’m being quiet, but I don’t know if that’s the same thing as less expressive. I don’t really watch myself talk, you know? And when I’m around people lately, I’m probably not giving them a lot to react to anyway, so it’s hard to tell.

I guess I haven’t noticed it clearly. If it’s happening, I don’t think anyone has explained it to me that way.
About how long have you been feeling that your supervisors are targeting you at work?

It’s been… a little over a year now, I think. Like, not just a few weeks or something.

If I try to place it, it started around maybe a year and a month ago. At first it was smaller things where I’d think, “That’s weird, why did they change my shift like that?” or “Why is that supervisor watching me so closely?” And I tried to tell myself it was probably nothing. But then it kept happening, or it felt like it kept lining up too much, and I couldn’t shake it.

So yeah… about 13 months, I guess. That’s when it really started feeling like they were targeting me and watching me on purpose.
Have these problems made it hard for you to keep up with your work or daily responsibilities?

Yeah… definitely. It’s gotten to the point where I can’t really pretend it’s just “stress” or being tired anymore.

At work, I’m still showing up, but I’m not keeping up the way I used to. I work as an aide, so there are rounds and charting and all these things you can’t really mess up or forget, and I’ve had coworkers having to double-check me more than they should. Like they’ll look back over my charting or make sure I actually completed rounds the right way, because I’ll get distracted or I’ll second-guess what I wrote, or I’ll just feel like I’m moving through fog. It’s embarrassing, honestly. I know people notice. And then that makes me feel worse, because I’m supposed to be helping, not becoming another problem somebody has to watch.

And at home it’s been worse. Bills pile up because I see them and I just don’t open them. Or I’ll open one and think, “I need to deal with this today,” and then I don’t, and then it becomes this whole thing I avoid. I’ve ignored friends so much that I don’t even know what to say back anymore. My apartment is… I mean, it’s bad. Not like a little messy. Like dishes, laundry, trash, stuff everywhere, and I keep telling myself I’ll do one small part of it, but then I just sit there looking at it and feel overwhelmed.

It got bad enough at work that employee health sent me for an emergency evaluation after I admitted I was thinking about suicide. I didn’t even mean to make it into this huge thing, but I guess when I said it out loud, they took it seriously. So… yeah, it’s definitely interfering with work and just basic life stuff.
During the times when you felt your supervisors were targeting you, were you also feeling depressed most of the time?

Yeah… I think so. Not just “down” like a bad day, but most of the time, especially when it gets really bad.

It’s like the two things feed into each other. When I’m more depressed, that’s when I’m also the most sure my supervisors are watching me, like through the cameras at work. I’ll start thinking every camera is being checked because of me, or that they’re waiting for me to mess something up so they can use it. And then because I’m thinking that, I get more frozen and more ashamed, and then I feel even lower.

And when I’m at my worst, I can’t even explain it right. Like if someone asks me what’s wrong, my words get all tangled. I’ll start a sentence and then lose where I was going, or I’ll try to explain why I think they’re watching me and it comes out messy, like I’m not making sense even though in my head it feels connected. Then I can see people looking confused or concerned, and that makes me feel even more like I’m being watched or judged.

So… yeah. During those times, I’m usually depressed most of the time, and the worse the depression gets, the stronger that feeling about them targeting me gets too.
Have you ever felt sure your supervisors were targeting you during a time when you were not depressed?

Yeah… there was a time like that. That’s part of what confused me, honestly, because I kept trying to tell myself it was only when I was really depressed, like when everything felt heavy and hopeless. But there was a stretch — maybe a few weeks — where I wasn’t in that deep, dark place the same way.

I mean, I wasn’t suddenly great or anything, but I could get up a little easier, I wasn’t just sitting there feeling completely crushed all day. I remember thinking, “Okay, maybe I’m coming out of it a little.” But even then, at work, I still felt sure the cameras were being used to watch me. Like I’d walk past one and immediately think, “They’re checking what I’m doing right now,” or if a supervisor came around, I’d feel like it wasn’t normal supervision, it was directed at me.

And I acted different because of it. I was guarded, like careful with every movement, careful what I said, trying not to look suspicious even though I didn’t even know what “suspicious” would be. I’d avoid certain areas if I thought I was being watched too much, or I’d get stiff when a supervisor was nearby.

So… yeah. It wasn’t only during the worst depression. There was at least that few-week period where my mood wasn’t as low, but I still believed they were monitoring me and targeting me.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there are prominent negative symptoms, which would help distinguish schizophrenia from delusional disorder and other psychotic or organic conditions.
doctor.question: Have you noticed yourself becoming less interested in being around other people?

target_item.name: Loss_of_Interest
target_item.manifestation: I used to sketch murals, cook for my friends, and play soccer on weekends, but now all of that feels pointless and I usually just ignore messages and stay in my apartment.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about reduced interest in socializing or being around other people, which directly matches loss of interest and withdrawal from previously enjoyed activities and social contact.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I have. I’ve kind of pulled away from people a lot, more than I even like admitting, I guess.

I used to be more… I don’t know, involved. Like I used to sketch murals, just for fun, and I’d get really into the ideas for them. I used to cook for friends too — not anything fancy all the time, but I liked having people over, making food, hanging out. And on weekends I’d play soccer, or at least I’d make plans to. It wasn’t like I was some super social person every second, but I had things I cared about, and people I’d actually want to see.

Now it all just feels kind of pointless. Like someone texts me and I’ll see it, and I know I should answer, but I just… don’t. Then hours go by, or days, and it feels harder to respond because now I have to explain why I didn’t. So I just ignore it. I end up staying in my apartment most of the time.

It’s not always that I hate people or anything. It’s more like being around them feels like too much effort, and the things I used to enjoy don’t really pull me in anymore. I know that sounds bad, but that’s kind of how it’s been.

doctor.question: About how long have you been feeling that your supervisors are targeting you at work?

target_item.name: Psychotic Symptoms Duration
target_item.manifestation: The beliefs about being watched and the disorganized behavior have been happening for about 1 year and 1 month.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking how long the persecutory belief about supervisors targeting him at work has been present, which is the duration of psychotic symptoms.

patient.answer:
It’s been… a little over a year now, I think. Like, not just a few weeks or something.

If I try to place it, it started around maybe a year and a month ago. At first it was smaller things where I’d think, “That’s weird, why did they change my shift like that?” or “Why is that supervisor watching me so closely?” And I tried to tell myself it was probably nothing. But then it kept happening, or it felt like it kept lining up too much, and I couldn’t shake it.

So yeah… about 13 months, I guess. That’s when it really started feeling like they were targeting me and watching me on purpose.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there has been a sustained decline in functioning, which would help distinguish schizophrenia from delusional disorder and other psychotic disorders.
doctor.question: Have these problems made it hard for you to keep up with your work or daily responsibilities?

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: I’ve needed coworkers to double-check my rounds and charting, and at home I’ve fallen behind on bills, ignored friends, and let my apartment get out of control. It got bad enough that employee health sent me for an emergency evaluation after I admitted I was thinking about suicide.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the symptoms have interfered with work and daily responsibilities, which directly matches functional impairment.

patient.answer:
Yeah… definitely. It’s gotten to the point where I can’t really pretend it’s just “stress” or being tired anymore.

At work, I’m still showing up, but I’m not keeping up the way I used to. I work as an aide, so there are rounds and charting and all these things you can’t really mess up or forget, and I’ve had coworkers having to double-check me more than they should. Like they’ll look back over my charting or make sure I actually completed rounds the right way, because I’ll get distracted or I’ll second-guess what I wrote, or I’ll just feel like I’m moving through fog. It’s embarrassing, honestly. I know people notice. And then that makes me feel worse, because I’m supposed to be helping, not becoming another problem somebody has to watch.

And at home it’s been worse. Bills pile up because I see them and I just don’t open them. Or I’ll open one and think, “I need to deal with this today,” and then I don’t, and then it becomes this whole thing I avoid. I’ve ignored friends so much that I don’t even know what to say back anymore. My apartment is… I mean, it’s bad. Not like a little messy. Like dishes, laundry, trash, stuff everywhere, and I keep telling myself I’ll do one small part of it, but then I just sit there looking at it and feel overwhelmed.

It got bad enough at work that employee health sent me for an emergency evaluation after I admitted I was thinking about suicide. I didn’t even mean to make it into this huge thing, but I guess when I said it out loud, they took it seriously. So… yeah, it’s definitely interfering with work and just basic life stuff.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the psychotic symptoms have persisted for at least one month in the absence of prominent mood symptoms, to distinguish schizophrenia from schizoaffective disorder.
doctor.question: During the times when you felt your supervisors were targeting you, were you also feeling depressed most of the time?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 1
target_item.manifestation: When the depression is at its worst, I’m also most convinced the supervisors are watching me through the cameras, and my speech gets so tangled that I can’t explain myself clearly.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the paranoid belief about supervisors targeting him occurred at the same time as feeling depressed most of the time, which directly concerns concurrent psychotic and depressive symptoms.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I think so. Not just “down” like a bad day, but most of the time, especially when it gets really bad.

It’s like the two things feed into each other. When I’m more depressed, that’s when I’m also the most sure my supervisors are watching me, like through the cameras at work. I’ll start thinking every camera is being checked because of me, or that they’re waiting for me to mess something up so they can use it. And then because I’m thinking that, I get more frozen and more ashamed, and then I feel even lower.

And when I’m at my worst, I can’t even explain it right. Like if someone asks me what’s wrong, my words get all tangled. I’ll start a sentence and then lose where I was going, or I’ll try to explain why I think they’re watching me and it comes out messy, like I’m not making sense even though in my head it feels connected. Then I can see people looking confused or concerned, and that makes me feel even more like I’m being watched or judged.

So… yeah. During those times, I’m usually depressed most of the time, and the worse the depression gets, the stronger that feeling about them targeting me gets too.

doctor.intent: Determine whether psychotic symptoms have ever occurred outside of depressive episodes, which best distinguishes schizoaffective disorder from schizophrenia or a mood-congruent psychotic depression picture.
doctor.question: Have you ever felt sure your supervisors were targeting you during a time when you were not depressed?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 3
target_item.manifestation: There was a stretch of a few weeks when I wasn’t in that deep depressed place, but I still believed the cameras and supervisors were monitoring me and I kept acting guarded at work.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the belief that supervisors were targeting him occurred during a period when he was not depressed, which directly assesses psychotic symptoms outside a major mood episode.

patient.answer:
Yeah… there was a time like that. That’s part of what confused me, honestly, because I kept trying to tell myself it was only when I was really depressed, like when everything felt heavy and hopeless. But there was a stretch — maybe a few weeks — where I wasn’t in that deep, dark place the same way.

I mean, I wasn’t suddenly great or anything, but I could get up a little easier, I wasn’t just sitting there feeling completely crushed all day. I remember thinking, “Okay, maybe I’m coming out of it a little.” But even then, at work, I still felt sure the cameras were being used to watch me. Like I’d walk past one and immediately think, “They’re checking what I’m doing right now,” or if a supervisor came around, I’d feel like it wasn’t normal supervision, it was directed at me.

And I acted different because of it. I was guarded, like careful with every movement, careful what I said, trying not to look suspicious even though I didn’t even know what “suspicious” would be. I’d avoid certain areas if I thought I was being watched too much, or I’d get stiff when a supervisor was nearby.

So… yeah. It wasn’t only during the worst depression. There was at least that few-week period where my mood wasn’t as low, but I still believed they were monitoring me and targeting me.

inference.note: Psychotic symptoms persisted for a few weeks outside of a major depressive episode, which argues against mood-congruent psychotic depression alone and supports a primary psychotic disorder. Functional decline, disorganized speech, social withdrawal/negative symptoms, and duration >1 year make F20.9 most likely; F25.9 remains possible because substantial depressive episodes are present for much of the illness; F22 is less likely given disorganization and negative symptoms. No evidence for a medical etiology was elicited, so F06.2 and F09 are less likely and dropped.

opening_question.intent: Learn the patient's main reason for seeking psychiatric care today
opening_question.question: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has persistent psychotic symptoms with persecutory delusions lasting over a year, plus disorganized speech and negative symptoms/social withdrawal with functional decline. A major depressive syndrome is present for much of the illness, but psychotic symptoms also persisted for at least a few weeks when the patient was not depressed, which supports schizoaffective disorder rather than a mood disorder with psychotic features. Compared with delusional disorder, there are additional schizophrenia-spectrum features beyond a circumscribed delusion, including disorganized speech, avolition/anhedonia, social withdrawal, and marked deterioration in functioning.
